text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Aston Villa and West Ham at Villa Park.

The hosts have picked up 16 points from their eight Premier League games this season, their highest tally at this stage of the competition since the 2009-10 campaign, and they will leapfrog Newcastle United into fifth if they avoid defeat here.
They have been formidable at home of late, winning their last 10 Premier League games at Villa Park.
The Hammers are also enjoying a strong start to the season, currently ninth but with the opportunity to go as high as fifth with a victory in this game.
They have had the upper hand in this fixture in recent years, unbeaten in 10 Premier League meetings between the sides, and David Moyes will be looking to come out on top against Villa again here.
Unai Emery makes just the one change from his team's last outing, a 1-1 draw away at Wolves before the international break, as Zaniolo comes in for Carlos while Kamara moves to centre-back.

Moyes names an unchanged starting XI from the side that drew 2-2 with Newcastle last time out as Antonio continues to lead the line, supported by Bowen, who has scored in all four of West Ham's away league games this season.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch at Villa Park ahead of this huge Premier League game.
The visitors kick us off and we are underway!
Martinez makes a great save to deny Bowen, though a delayed flag goes up for offside and the goal would not have counted anyway.
It has been a lively start at Villa Park, with both teams looking to get on top of the early exchanges.

West Ham have named the same starting XI in five consecutive Premier League games for the first time since the 1993-94 season, when they named the same starting XI in six consecutive Premier League games.
Douglas Luiz gets down the right before fizzing a cross into the penalty area, though the delivery is too close to Areola and the West Ham goalkeeper intercepts it.
10 minutes on the clock at Villa Park, and neither side has been able to fashion a real clear-cut chance so far.
Bowen wriggles into the Villa box, but he gets himself in a bit of a tangle and nudges the ball out of play.
SAVE! Douglas Luiz's curling effort from distance looks to be flying into the top corner, until Areola makes an acrobatic stop to tip it wide at full stretch.
That is the closest either team has come so far.
Bowen's dipping drive is gathered relatively comfortably by Martinez down to his right.
A neat move gives Digne the ball on the left of the box, but his cross is cut out by a well-placed Ward-Prowse.
WHAT A MISS! Another slick passage of play sees Diaby pick out Watkins, who takes a touch before lashing at goal.
It looks like he cannot miss, but he somehow manages to fire past the left post and harmlessly wide.
That is a huge let-off for the visitors!
West Ham have won their last three league matches at Villa Park, but they have never won four consecutive league matches away at Villa.
The Villans are on top at the moment, with West Ham largely penned back deep in their own half.
Can the hosts take advantage of this spell of pressure?
Villa have lost their last three Premier League home games against West Ham, as many as they had in their first 21 against them (nine wins, nine draws).
25 minutes gone at Villa Park and while the hosts have been on top, they have not yet found a way through this Hammers defence.
Diaby drags a shot well wide of the target from 25 yards out.
A player of his quality will expect to have done better there.
GOAL!!! DOUGLAS LUIZ FIRES VILLA IN FRONT!!! The hosts have been on top and now they have netted the opener, with Watkins showing great composure to cut the ball back for Douglas Luiz.
The midfielder hits it first time, and while Areola gets down to his right to try and save, the power on the effort takes it in to put the hosts 1-0 up!
Watkins did well to play the ball back for Douglas Luiz to lash home.
Villa are smelling blood here as Watkins blasts a shot into the side netting, before McGinn's deflected shot goes over moments later.

events.action: blasts a shot into the side net

text: Douglas Luiz has scored in each of his last six Premier League matches at Villa Park (six goals).
He is the first Villa player to achieve this feat.
A nicely worked free-kick routine opens up the space for McGinn to shoot from distance, but the Scotland international fires well wide.
Although they lost their last away league game 3-1 at Liverpool, West Ham have won two of their last three such matches, as many as their previous 18 on the road beforehand (four draws, 12 defeats).
Alvarez's powerful drive comes off the arm of Konsa, inches away from penalty area.
Villa have been very fortunate there, though Ward-Prowse is standing over the resulting free-kick.
Ward-Prowse, usually so dangerous from dead-ball situations, sends his free-kick off the wall, much to the home fans' relief.
Antonio's shot from a tight angle smashes into the side netting.
It has been a decent spell for the Hammers, though they remain a goal down.
There will be two minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-0 WEST HAM
Villa take a deserved 1-0 lead into the break after Douglas Luiz netted for the sixth home Premier League game in a row to put them ahead.
They had been threatening, and with half an hour gone, Watkins cut the ball back for Douglas Luiz to thump home.
The midfielder had already gone close with a long-range curler, while Watkins spurned a golden opportunity shortly after as he shot wide.
West Ham improved before the break, though they have it all to do in the second half if they are to come away with a result.
His team did show signs of life late in that first half, but Moyes will surely be very unhappy with his side's display so far.
He has options on the bench with the likes of Kudus and Benrahma, so how long will he leave it before looking to his substitutes?
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half.

Douglas Luiz's first-half opener was his 15th Premier League goal, which takes him to number 15 on the list of Brazilians with the most goals in the competition, above Robinho, Elano, Geovanni and David Luiz (all on 14).
PENALTY TO VILLA!!! Paqueta gives the ball away in a terrible area and Konsa races onto it, taking a touch towards the byline.
Alvarez tries to nip the ball away from Konsa but ends up taking the former Brentford man out, and the referee takes a moment before pointing to the spot!
DOUGLAS LUIZ SCORES FROM THE SPOT!!! The midfielder grabs his second of the game as he smashes his penalty down the middle, and Villa are 2-0 up! It is a long way back for West Ham now.
No player in the Premier League this season has scored more penalties than Douglas Luiz's three (level with Mohamed Salah).
Emerson cynically wipes out Cash and receives a yellow card for his troubles.
That is his fifth booking of the season and therefore, he will miss next weekend's game against Everton.
GOAL!!! WEST HAM ARE BACK IN IT!!! Bowen cuts onto his left foot before firing goalwards from outside the box, receiving a huge slice of luck as the shot takes a wicked deflection off Digne.
It completely wrongfoots Martinez and flies into the bottom corner, and the score is now 2-1 to Villa!
Alvarez laid the ball off to Bowen before the deflection took the ball into the back of the net.
Bowen has joined Thierry Henry and Salah as the only players to score in each of their first five away appearances from the start of a season in the Premier League.
Half an hour left at Villa Park, and the hosts appear a little nervy having looked so comfortable prior to Bowen's goal.
Can they steady the ship to secure the three points?
There is a brief pause in play for Zaniolo to receive treatment for a head injury, though he is swiftly back to his feet.
Cash makes a big block to nod Aguerd's acrobatic volley over the crossbar and out for a corner.
Bowen sends a header well over the crossbar from Ward-Prowse's corner delivery.
Moyes looks to his bench for the first time, bringing on Kudus for Soucek.
20 minutes to play at Villa Park, and the visitors are ramping up their search for an equaliser.
West Ham win a couple of corners in quick succession, though Emery's men are able to scramble them away as their 2-1 lead remains intact.
GOAL!!! WATKINS PUTS VILLA 3-1 UP!!! McGinn lofts a delightful throughball over the top for Watkins, who races onto it before a couple of stepovers create the space to let fly.
The power on the strike gives Areola no chance, rifling into the foot of the net to potentially put this game beyond West Ham's reach!
McGinn's pass was excellent to pick out Watkins before the striker thumped home.
Emery makes his first change, replacing Zaniolo with Bailey.
Bowen has scored more Premier League goals against Villa than any other side with five.
In his career across all competitions, he has only scored more goals against Preston North End and Queens Park Rangers - six goals against each.
Antonio stings the palms of Martinez with a fierce drive as the visitors try to find a way to reduce the deficit again.

Bowen is nearly the beneficiary of another deflection as his cross takes a nick before arrowing towards the top corner, though the ball goes the wrong side of the bar for West Ham and onto the roof of the net.
This is the second time Watkins has both scored and assisted in a Premier League game this season, the first player to do so more than once this term.
Emery makes a substitution as he looks to get his team over the line, with Tielemans coming on for Diaby.
Paqueta makes way for Ings.
No team in the Premier League has had more instances of a player scoring a brace or more this season than Villa with three.
Watkins, Cash and Douglas Luiz have all scored two or more goals in a single league match this season.
GOAL!!! BAILEY MAKES IT 4-1!!! Just moments after coming off the bench, Bailey collects the ball off Tielemans before some nifty footwork takes him past Aguerd.
He keeps his composure to fire past Areola to surely make the points safe.
Tielemans fed the ball into Bailey before he brilliantly did the rest.
Antonio is replaced by Fornals.
We are into seven minutes of additional time at the end of this game, and Villa are still pressing to add to the scoreline.
Kudus' shot from a difficult angle is easily saved by Martinez.
Coufal is down receiving treatment for a head injury after a coming-together with Digne.
After receiving some medical attention, Coufal is back on his feet and play has resumed.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 4-1 WEST HAM
The full-time whistle blows to bring a dominant Villa performance to an end as they claim a 4-1 win over West Ham, their first victory against the Hammers since the 2014-15 campaign.
Douglas Luiz put Emery's men in control as he thumped home the opener with half an hour on the clock before scoring from the spot after Konsa was felled by Alvarez.
West Ham did pull a goal back through Ward-Prowse's deflected strike, but Watkins would restore Villa's two-goal advantage with an emphatic finish before Bailey capped the win off the bench.
The win takes Villa up to fifth, just two points off leaders Manchester City, while defeat means West Ham remain ninth.
Both sides are in European action next week, when Villa travel to take on AZ in the Europa Conference League while the Hammers will play away at Olympiacos in the Europa League.
That is all from us at Villa Park, so thanks for tuning in and goodbye!
